firstFour.method: Read-only TAR/ZIP byte comparison and static text inspection. No package code imports/execution, no dynamic deobfuscation, no payload URL requests, no rule changes. Miss-shape explanations are bounded static inferences.

staticIndicators: obfuscated code appended to the ordinary CommonJS bundle

controls.scope: Read-only triage of the two alerted controls from the frozen 20-version run; no scanner changes, source execution or new sample selection.

controls.name: @electron/get
controls.ruleEvidence: The rule removes the @electron scope, compares get against popular-package names, and reports edit distance 2 to jest. This is the official Electron artifact downloader, not a jest lookalike package.

additionalFinding.explanation: The package genuinely invokes a subprocess to identify the host architecture. That Medium capability finding accounts for the additional eight-point deduction in deep mode; the High package-name finding is the false positive.

controls.name: dotenv
controls.ruleEvidence: SSH_KEY_PATTERN only checks for a private-key BEGIN header. The README's multiline-variable documentation contains explicitly abbreviated illustrative key blocks with ellipses, not a complete credential. The rule calls this an exposed SSH key and the Critical severity forces dangerous.

packageEvidence.snippet: If you need multiline variables, for example private keys, those are now supported

scannerEvidence.explanation: The regex matches only the BEGIN marker, without requiring a complete key body or checking documentation-placeholder context.
Any marker match emits the Critical secret-exposure finding.

controls.redaction: No full private-key contents reproduced; examples are placeholders and snippets are sanitized further.
